text:
Elena: Hi all, quick onboarding question. I start next Wed — can I add my partner to health/dental right away? Also I have a refundable deposit for my apartment move and need an expense advance for the flight — who handles advances? 

Maya (People Ops): Welcome, Elena! :wave: For dependents: you have a 30-day enrollment window from your start date to add dependents (partner, kids). You need to upload proof (marriage certificate, domestic partnership affidavit, or birth certificates) to the benefits portal.

Derek (Benefits): Adding detail: coverage effective date follows company standard: 1st of the month after 30 days. But if you enroll within the 30-day window we can request an exception for retro coverage back to your start date in certain cases (e.g., loss of previous coverage). Send proof and a short note explaining timing.

Elena: Thanks — I might need retro because my partner's COBRA ends the day before I start. What's the exception process? And does domestic partnership count the same as spouse for premiums?

Derek (Benefits): If COBRA ends immediately before your start, include the COBRA end date in your portal upload and tag it "retro request". Benefits team reviews and we escalate to carrier if needed. Domestic partners are allowed but premium structure depends on carrier; some partners fall under same dependent tier, others are rated differently. We can confirm exact premium once you enter dependent info.

Anya (Payroll): For advances: payroll handles employee advances when approved by hiring manager. Ask your manager to approve an "Expense Advance" and email payroll@redwood.example with subject: "ADVANCE - Elena - Relocation Flight - <offerID>". We'll process on the next business day after approval. Note: advances are recovered over next 2 pay cycles unless you request a different schedule.

Elena: Good to know. For proof docs, is scanned PDF OK or do you need originals? Also any special coding for the advance so finance puts it under relocation expense?

Maya (People Ops): Scanned PDFs with a legible header/footer are fine. Upload to the benefits portal under "Dependent Documentation". For the advance, in the email subject include the word "Relocation" and your offer ID; payroll will assign the relocation expense code when they create the advance. CC your hiring manager and finance@redwood.example.

Derek (Benefits): One more note: for HSA eligibility, if you add a dependent, contribution limits remain per IRS rules (family vs individual). If you plan to open HSA, set it up before the first payroll contribution. Link to HSA FAQ: https://benefits.redwood.example/hsa-faq

Benefits Bot: Document uploaded (ID 33412) by Elena. Status: pending manual review.

Elena: Perfect. Last Q: I submitted W-4 but my state form shows single by default. Can payroll change it to married filing jointly if I provide proof?

Anya (Payroll): We can update your state/federal withholding forms if you upload the updated W-4 and state form to the payroll portal. If you prefer, DM me and I can walk through the fields. Remember changes affect future pay runs, not retro pay.

Elena: Appreciate the help! I'll upload docs today and ask my manager to OK the advance. :)

Maya (People Ops): Welcome again, Elena — ping us if anything stalls. We'll follow up once benefits review completes. :raised_hands:
